## New cross-domain connections
- **[2026-11-13] Burry rates Unity a "Castle" against AI, a tier above Chapel, on the strength of Unity AI, Vector and Commerce. Fred is a Unity user, and the wiki's notes on his own game are a first-hand data point on the engine part of that rating: his setup routes around Unity AI and keeps the exit free.** [[finance/investor-letters/source-burry-sw50-part2-productivity-cybersecurity-2026-05-28]] has Unity at Castle, 2.13x P/IV15, rank 35 of 50, score 14.9, not owned, with Burry "watching for it to fall to ~1x". [[ai-tech/unity-development-with-claude-code]] records three facts that bear on it. The official Unity MCP server sits inside Unity AI and needs a Cloud-connected project plus a Unity AI trial or subscription; Fred registered the free community CoplayDev bridge instead, and the official relay is not registered. The simulation core has no `UnityEngine` types, so "the engine choice stays reversible", and the project already flipped Godot 4 → Unity 6 (D-022 → D-032) without touching rules code. And the GDD's own view is that Unity needs more setup for agent work than Godot would. [[games/project-terrain-autobattler]] adds that all development is done by Claude Code. So on this project the AI work is done by a frontier-lab agent through a free bridge, Unity is paid nothing for AI, and lock-in is thin by design. Limits: this is one pre-revenue hobby project, the editor side was still unverified on 09-30, and it says nothing about Vector (ads) or Commerce, which Fred's game does not touch and which the Burry page names as most of the moat. Neither page links the other, Finance has no Unity idea page, and nothing in Finance notes that Fred uses the product. **Next step, when Unity 6 is installed:** record on the Unity page which bridge ended up in use and whether any paid Unity AI feature was needed. That is the line a Unity idea page would cite if the price reaches Burry's ~1x.

- **[2026-11-13] Work's Workday debate ends on a prediction with no example: the winner is whoever already holds the accountability and configuration layer and puts agents on top of it. The Capital Allocators episode added on 11-07 is a vendor describing that move in another vertical, and it is filed only under Podcasts.** In [[work/source-workday-disruption-debate-2026]], LaRocque puts the moat in compliance accountability ($24.5B across 539 deals in Workday-competitive categories, none through the F500 ceiling) and Turnbull puts it in the config framework, "exactly the boundaries agents need". Every voice on the page is from HR tech. Fred's takeaway 3 says the SaaS → SaS shift "applies beyond HR" and cites no case outside HR. [[podcasts/podcast-capital-allocators-ai-tools-for-the-investment-firm-ben-harrison]] is that case: Ben Harrison of Intapp (DealCloud co-founder) on "firm AI", agents that run a firm's procedures on its institutional memory "within governance and confidentiality limits", for private-markets and professional-services firms, with a chapter on parallels from law and consulting. It is the same moat claim (proprietary records, workflow integration, governance) made by an incumbent in a different regulated vertical. The podcast page links the episode to the general "AI kills SaaS" debate, the BofA episode and Sacerdote, not to Work, and [[work/overview]] has had no new source since May. Caveats: Harrison is talking his own book, and the page was built from the episode listing, not a transcript, so it holds no numbers. The Work page's tension table has three columns of opinion and no evidence from another vertical. The two chapters that could supply some are 12:12 (what actually slows adoption in financial services) and 25:04 (whether agents cut junior headcount or only slow hiring); the first tests LaRocque's "compliance cannot be automated" against Schmidt's "deploy in 1 month". The same incumbent-keeps-the-records argument sits under the live SAP and Accenture holdings (see 09-25 and 11-01), so a second vertical is evidence for or against those too.

None today. No older ideas resolved, and no new podcast books.

## New cross-domain connections
- **[2026-11-12] Lightfin's adaptation page has three tracks. The two that would reach an audience, book and video, have been "Exploring" since April because each waits on a publishing or production decision. The N.D. Austin episode Fred finished this week describes a fourth format that needs neither: stage one case as a one-off live mystery for a few children.** [[lightfin/adaptation-overview]] lists book, video and story expansion, with games as "future". [[lightfin/story-bible]] says audience participation is "core to the format, not incidental", yet the only participation the show has is the 15-second pause before the reveal. [[podcasts/podcast-death-sex-and-money-real-life-willy-wonka-tony-hawk]] gives a working method in three parts. Open with unexplained objects: Hawk's staff found a shovel, a locked briefcase and keys on their desks. Build from what the players already share: the funeral board game was assembled from mechanics the friends had played for years. End it for good: that game was played once and buried. [[lightfin/ep-000-treasure-of-the-esperanza]] already supplies all three. It has planted gold coins in a desk drawer, two suspects to question (Sidney Stonefish and Blue Marlin), and a treasure to dig up at the end. The podcast page's own note links Austin to game design in general and to the Yousef episode; it does not mention Lightfin. A live case would also test something the book track assumes and has never checked: that 5–8s only "guess along" while 9–13s can follow a clue trail, which is the whole basis for the picture-book and chapter-book split. It is also a paper prototype for the game track in [[games/overview]]. **Smallest next step:** add "Track 4: live case (one-off)" to the adaptation page's options and write Case 0 as three clue stations plus the planted-coin reveal. Run it once with children from both age bands and note which clues each band solved without help.

- **[2026-11-12] Finance's stablecoin page argues that Washington is building a captive buyer of Treasury bills out of stablecoin demand. It treats that demand as one number. This week's first podcast pick, Scam Inc, is about one part of it: scam compounds that move stolen money over crypto rails.** [[finance/investor-letters/source-bond-market-bessent-stablecoins-2026-09-02]] puts Tether at about $183.6bn of a $308bn market, with about $140.6bn in Treasury-linked reserves, and quotes Bessent's projection of 10x growth by 2030. It never asks who holds the tokens. [[podcasts/suggestions]] (week of 2026-11-12) describes Scam Inc as an eight-part Economist series on the pig-butchering economy in Southeast Asia, "including how stolen money is laundered through crypto rails". From outside the wiki, and to be checked against the series: UNODC reporting has named USDT, mostly on Tron, as the preferred rail for those networks. If that holds, the largest holder in the Treasury-buyer thesis is also the issuer most exposed to enforcement, and the 10x path depends on demand that the same government wants to grow and to police. Neither side is in the wiki. [[crypto/crypto-overview]] tracks only delta-neutral designs (USDN, USDe), and [[crypto/defi-watchlist]] links the Bessent page for reserve exposure only. This is a different gap from the 10-22 entry, which was about exploit risk in Fred's own tokens. **If Fred listens:** note which token and chain the series names and any estimate of the sums involved, and add them to the Bessent page as a caveat on the quality of the demand.
